text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Investment group Robeco talks with pension fund manager Beon Pensioen en Vermogensbeheer on possible alliance. (p1)
- Merchant bank MeesPierson chairman Joost Kuiper's remarks about scaling down ambitions causes concern among the bank's employees. (p1)
- World's largest reinsurer Muenchener Rueck of Germany buys 12 pct stake in ASRV, the newly-formed holding of Stad Rotterdam and De Amersfoortse. (p1)
- Realty fund KNSF's shares rocket after 1 to 2000 split. (p1)
- Raised bid from Dfl 12.50 to Dfl 13,75 is to speed up the takeover of biotech concern MoGen. (p3)
- Philips Electroncis sells its stakes in three financial institutions among which bank Mendes Gans. (p3)
- Retailer Ahold reports strong growth in Q1 turnover and profits. (p5)
- The sale of the Dutch State's 76 pct stake in Schiphol Airport not earlier than in two years' time. (p6)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Coalition agreement breaks on possibility for employers to pay workers below minimum wages. (p1)
- Businesses lose billions of guilders on new automation projects, appears from survey. (p2)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier makes Microsoft's technology the cornerstone of its electronic information products. (p13)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Some 3,000 people per year die as a result of medical errors according to a study. (p3)
- Philips Electronics is expecting positive effects from the introduction of the European single currency Euro. (p23)
- Insurer Aegon and pensionfund PGGM's realty joint venture Amvast is to sell part of its realty portfolio. (p23)
- Food and detergent group Unilever targets at the poor population of Asia and South America for selling its detergents. (p25)
TROUW
- Finance company for developing countries FMO seeks to develop new instruments to help small Dutch companies to invest in poor countries. (p6)
- Shareholder lobbygroup VEB will demand dredger Boskalis' board member J. Kraaijeveld van Hemert's resignation because of mismanagement. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Health minister Els Borst wants yet to support European guideline for general ban on tobacco ads. (p3)
- Retail and services group Vendex International sees the list of possible takeover candidates getting shorter. (p13)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
